core.title: Validate artifact names against format, semantic and technical rules
core.given: A plan artifact or slice manifest, an acceptance artifact, a contract, or a consumer declares, references, uses or validates an artifact name
core.when: that name, a reference to it, or its contract or its declared contract URN is added, used or changed
core.then: The artifact name must pass all three validation rule categories — format, semantic and technical.
prefer: Format: theme lowercase with no separators; category/aspect/variant kebab-case; ':' for descent (hierarchy levels); '.' for variants.
Semantic: theme from the approved taxonomy; each hierarchy level adds value; aspect a concrete noun; variant a state/type/facet.
Technical: a contract exists at the contract location derived from the name by splitting it on ':' and '.'; the URN it declares is the contract URN of the name.
The URN matches the name exactly, and all consumers reference that same name.
avoid: A URN that differs in any way from the name.
Consumers referencing a different spelling or alias of the name.
Hierarchy levels that add no value.
core.why: The name is the join key between plans, contracts and consumers; deriving format, meaning and file path from one name lets contracts be located mechanically and catches drift.
evidence: Each artifact name meets the format rule (lowercase theme without separators, kebab-case category/aspect/variant, ':' descent, '.' variants).
Theme is in the approved taxonomy; levels add value, aspect is a concrete noun, variant is a state/type/facet, no deep variant nesting; URN matches the name exactly.
The contract at the profile's contract location for the name exists, the URN it declares equals the contract URN of the name, and all consumer references use the identical name.
verification: Check scope: an artifact name is validated against exactly three categories — format, semantic and technical — wherever it is declared, referenced, used or validated. Activation location examples are illustrative only, not scope gates: any file that declares or references an artifact name is in scope.

Format check: theme segment lowercase with no separators; category/aspect/variant segments kebab-case; ':' separates hierarchy levels (descent) and '.' separates variants. Do not add restrictions beyond lowercase/no separators (the source does not further restrict the theme alphabet, e.g. digits).

Semantic checks: theme membership is checked against the approved taxonomy, which is maintained outside this rule; 'each hierarchy level adds value', 'aspect is a concrete noun', 'variant is a state/type/facet' and 'no deep variant nesting' are llm_judged — no numeric nesting threshold is given; 'the URN matches the name exactly' is a deterministic string equality.

Technical check: split the name on ':' and '.' to obtain its segments; require the contract at the profile's contract location for those segments to exist; require the URN it declares, carried in the profile's contract identity field, to equal the contract URN of the name exactly; collect all consumer references and require the identical name. The rule does not fix how segments join into the contract location — use the repository's existing contract layout rather than inventing one.
The check also applies to existing, unchanged artifact names when they are newly referenced or their contract changes.

Observability: needs a diff-level observer that extracts artifact names and their references, plus contract URN and contract-location changes, whether or not the name itself changed; a name validator or review reporting a format, semantic or technical violation on any existing name is also a trigger.

values: artifact name declared, referenced or used
contract location or declared URN changed
consumer reference to an artifact added or changed

fires: A new artifact name is declared in a produce/consume list.
An existing artifact is renamed or gets a variant.
A consumer adopts an existing, unchanged artifact name whose contract is missing.
A contract's declared URN or file location is edited so it no longer matches the artifact name, without renaming the artifact.
A contract whose declared URN carries an artifact name is authored or referenced.
A validator or review reports a violation on any existing artifact name.
doesNotFire: Edits to acceptance prose that neither declare, reference nor change any artifact name or its contract.
Changes to identifiers that are not artifact names (e.g. test function names, local variables).

The identity field of the contract artifact: the field a contract carries that declares its own URN (a self-declaration of contract identity, not a source/test binding).

neutralityNotes: The artifact-name grammar itself (theme:category:aspect.variant, ':' descent, '.' variants, kebab-case, approved taxonomy, URN-equals-name) is the subject of the convention and contains no stack reference, so it stays in the core verbatim. The only concrete anchors — the contract file pattern (contracts/{segments}.schema.json), the contract URN shape (urn:contract:{artifact_name}) and the identity field carrying it ($id) — are supplied by the profile via layout.contract_paths#contract_file, urn.contract and urn.grammar#contract_identity_field (the contract's self-declared identity is grammar of the contract artifact, not a source/test binding, so the urn.binding.* key is not used). The example activation globs and the finding id remain Bun-only. The approved taxonomy contents, any numeric nesting threshold and the segment-to-path join are unspecified by the source; that deference is preserved in core:verification rather than neutralized into new obligations. 'wagon' in the Bun given is the stack's plan-level slice manifest; the core uses the plan-artifact role, and the activation note ('any file that declares or references an artifact name is in scope') keeps the obligation identical. No per-rule severity or disposition exists in bun.json, so none was invented.
